goal: Document the complete checkout flow from pricing page to payment confirmation
projectContext:
**Target audience**: Developers integrating Stripe payments into their applications
**Key workflow**: Selecting a plan, entering payment details, and completing checkout
**Non-obvious behaviors / terminology**: Stripe uses 'Payment Intents' for one-time payments and 'Subscriptions' for recurring billing. Test mode uses card number 4242 4242 4242 4242.

steps.observation: The pricing page loaded. It shows three main plans: Integrated (2.9% + 30c per transaction), Customized (custom pricing), and a comparison table below. There's a header with 'Products', 'Solutions', 'Developers', 'Resources', and 'Pricing' nav items. A prominent 'Start now' button appears next to each plan.

steps.action: Scroll down to see all pricing plans
steps.observation: Scrolled down to reveal the full pricing comparison table. Three tiers visible: 'Integrated' for startups (2.9% + 30c), 'Customized' for large volumes (custom pricing with volume discounts), and feature comparison rows showing: recurring billing, invoicing, tax calculation, fraud prevention (Radar), and 24/7 support. Each row shows checkmarks for included features.

steps.action: Click 'Start now' button under the Integrated plan
steps.observation: Clicked the 'Start now' button for the Integrated plan. The page navigated to the Stripe registration form. Agent reasoning: The Integrated plan is the most common starting point for new users.

The registration page shows a form with fields: Email, Full name, Country, and Password. There's also 'Sign in' link for existing users and social sign-up options (Google). The page has a clean layout with Stripe branding and a brief description: 'Start accepting payments in minutes.'
Filled in the email field with 'test@example.com'. The field accepted the input and showed a green checkmark validation indicator.

steps.action: Fill form: entered full name and selected country
steps.observation: Filled 'Full name' with 'Test User' and selected 'United States' from the country dropdown. The country dropdown is a searchable select with all countries listed alphabetically.

steps.action: Fill form: entered password and submitted
steps.observation: Entered a password and clicked 'Create account'. Password field shows strength indicator. Form submitted successfully and redirected to the Stripe Dashboard onboarding flow.

The onboarding page shows a step-by-step setup wizard. Current step: 'Activate payments'. There are 4 steps visible: 1) Add business details, 2) Add bank account, 3) Activate payments, 4) Start accepting payments. A progress bar at the top shows 25% completion.

steps.action: Scroll down to see onboarding details
steps.observation: Below the steps, there's a 'Test mode' toggle prominently displayed with explanation text: 'Use test mode to simulate transactions without processing real payments. Toggle to live mode when ready to accept real payments.' Test mode is currently ON (orange indicator).

Navigated to the Payments section. The page shows an empty state: 'No payments yet. Create a test payment to see how it works.' There's a blue 'Create payment' button. Left sidebar shows: Home, Payments, Balances, Customers, Products, and more items. 'TEST MODE' badge is visible in the header.

A modal appeared titled 'Create a payment'. Fields shown: Amount (pre-filled with $10.00), Currency (USD dropdown), Description (optional), Customer (optional autocomplete), Payment method section with card input fields. The modal has 'Create' and 'Cancel' buttons at the bottom.

steps.action: Fill form: entered amount $25.00 and test card number
steps.observation: Changed amount to $25.00. Entered test card number 4242 4242 4242 4242, expiry 12/25, CVC 123. A help tooltip appeared next to the card field: 'Use test card numbers to simulate different scenarios.' The form validated all fields with green checkmarks.

steps.action: Click 'Create' to submit the test payment
steps.observation: Payment created successfully. The modal closed and the payments list now shows one entry: '$25.00 USD — Succeeded' with a green status badge. Timestamp shows 'Just now'. The payment ID (pi_...) is visible as a clickable link.

steps.action: Click on the payment to view details
steps.observation: Payment detail page shows: Status 'Succeeded' (green), Amount $25.00 USD, Payment method 'Visa ending in 4242', Timeline with events (Payment created, Payment succeeded), Risk evaluation 'Normal' (green), and metadata section. There's a 'Refund' button in the top right and tabs for Overview, Events, and Logs.

steps.action: Done: Completed exploration of Stripe checkout and payment flow
steps.observation: Successfully explored the complete Stripe flow: pricing page with plan comparison, account registration, dashboard onboarding with test mode, creating a test payment with card details, and viewing payment details with status and timeline. Key flows documented: plan selection, registration, test mode setup, payment creation, and payment detail view.
